To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel load flow based approach is proposed to efficiently and realistically assess the availability of reconfigurable systems, and that a novel metric and a real time ranking procedure for assessing maintenance adequacy and prioritizing maintenance tasks are introduced.

a novel load flow based simulation approach is introduced to simplify the availability analysis of realistic engineering systems, a novel metric for assessing the inadequacy of maintenance resources is introduced, and a novel real time component ranking algorithm is introduced.

a new simulation technique has been developed for availability assessment of re-configurable systems with inter-dependencies and that the new technique is simpler and more efficient than other techniques.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of efficient simulation tools for availability assessment and maintenance optimisation of engineering systems.
the efficient availability assessment of reconfigured engineering systems with multi state components and complex interdependencies, which may also be subjected to external phenomena.
the development of a novel simulation based methodology for assessing the availability of reconfigurable engineering systems with complex topologies and interdependencies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach is a significant step in simplifying the availability assessment of reconfigured multi state systems, and that the approach is applicable to a wide range of systems.
the proposed approach is more efficient, intuitive, and robust to human induced error than other Monte Carlo simulation based approaches for availability assessment of complex systems.
the proposed approach is more efficient than the existing approaches for availability assessment of realistic multi state systems with component interdependencies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel load flow based approach for the availability assessment of multi commodity flow systems.
the load flow approach provides a simple, efficient, and generally applicable simulation technique for availability assessment of realistic systems with interdependencies and complex topologies.
the load flow simulation approach proposed here is a simple and generally applicable technique to assess the availability of realistic engineering systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed load flow simulation approach can be used to efficiently assess the availability of realistic systems with complex topology, multi-state behaviour, and component interdependencies.
the availability assessment of engineering systems with complex topologies can be performed efficiently using load flow simulation techniques.
a load flow simulation approach can be used for efficient availability assessment of reconfiguration systems with interdependencies.
